title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1: Yes—GLP erred in ruling the later complaint out of order on the ground that Presbytery had already dealt with all issues; GLP conflated the earlier complaint (SJC 2010-28) with the later one. Issue 2: No—GLP did not err in declining to investigate TE Dupee under BCO 31-2, because Dupee reported as committee chairman and the statement was the committee's authorized report, not his personal statement. Overall: The Complaint is denied; no investigation or other relief ordered.
first_summary: The SJC denied a minister's complaint against Great Lakes Presbytery's refusal to investigate another minister under BCO 31-2. The SJC held that the accused minister was acting as committee chairman when he made the statement and therefore had immunity from personal investigation; the complaint was without merit.
summary: The SJC denied a minister's complaint challenging Presbytery's out-of-order dismissal of his request for a BCO 31-2 investigation of another minister. Although the SJC agreed Presbytery wrongly said it had already decided all issues—the earlier complaint (SJC 2010-28) was distinct—it upheld the refusal to investigate. The accused minister had delivered an authorized committee report as chairman; absent evidence he exceeded that authorization, his statements were the committee's, not personal, and BCO 31-2 did not require investigation.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2011-02, Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery, decided by the SJC at the 40th GA. Adopted at lines 60–64: written by TE Dominic Aquila with amendments by the full SJC; 23 concurring, 1 absent.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 15–33: TE Gonzales complained that GLP wrongly ruled out of order his complaint seeking a BCO 31-2 investigation of TE David Dupee. GLP had declined the investigation on Nov. 13, 2010, and on Jan. 8, 2011 ruled the complaint out of order saying it had already dealt with all issues.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 35–58: Issue 1 answered Yes—GLP erred by conflating this complaint with SJC 2010-28; Issue 2 answered No—GLP did not err in refusing to investigate Dupee because he reported as committee chairman and the statement was the committee's authorized report, not personal. The complaint was denied.

evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 25 and 50 reference SJC 2010-28, the earlier complaint. Its result is not supplied and is not needed to decide this complaint; no other incorporated decision appears.
